# Cold Brew Coffee Ratio

Cold brew needs a stronger ratio than hot coffee because cold water extracts slowly over many hours in the fridge.

A concentrate made at one part coffee to five parts water is easy to dilute later with milk or water to taste.

Steep the grounds for twelve to eighteen hours, then filter twice through a paper filter to remove the fine sediment that makes it muddy.

Coarse grounds work best because fine grounds over-extract during the long steep and clog the filter when you try to strain it.

Store the finished concentrate in a sealed jar in the refrigerator and drink it within a week for the best flavour.
